definitions: To give shelter or refuge to someone, especially a criminal.
To keep a thought or feeling, typically a negative one, in one's mind for a long time.
To carry or contain a germ or disease.
To shelter a ship or boat in a harbour.
examples: He was accused of harbouring a fugitive.
She continues to harbour a grudge.
The stagnant water can harbour bacteria.
The bay harbours many small vessels.
